{{short description|Theorem in queueing theory}}
In [[queueing theory]], a discipline within the mathematical [[probability theory|theory of probability]], '''Burke's theorem''' (sometimes the '''Burke's output theorem'''<ref>{{Cite journal | last1 = Walrand | first1 = J. | author-link1 = Jean Walrand| title = A probabilistic look at networks of quasi-reversible queues | doi = 10.1109/TIT.1983.1056762 | journal = IEEE Transactions on Information Theory | volume = 29 | issue = 6 | pages = 825–831 | year = 1983 | s2cid = 216943 }}</ref>) is a [[theorem]] (stated and demonstrated by [[Paul J. Burke]] while working at [[Bell Telephone Laboratories]]) asserting that, for the [[M/M/1 queue]], [[M/M/c queue]] or [[M/M/∞ queue]] in the steady state with arrivals is a [[Poisson process]] with rate parameter λ:

# The departure process is a Poisson process with rate parameter&nbsp;λ.
# At time ''t'' the number of customers in the queue is independent of the departure process prior to time&nbsp;''t''.

==Proof==
Burke first published this theorem along with a proof in 1956.<ref>{{Cite journal | last1 = Burke | first1 = P. J. | s2cid = 55089958 | title = The Output of a Queuing System | doi = 10.1287/opre.4.6.699 | journal = Operations Research | volume = 4 | issue = 6 | pages = 699–704 | year = 1956 }}</ref> The theorem was anticipated but not proved by O'Brien (1954) and Morse (1955).<ref name="connell">{{Cite journal | last1 = O'Connell | first1 = N. | last2 = Yor | first2 = M. | title = Brownian analogues of Burke's theorem | doi = 10.1016/S0304-4149(01)00119-3 | journal = Stochastic Processes and Their Applications | volume = 96 | issue = 2 | pages = 285–298 | date=December 2001 | doi-access = free }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal | doi = 10.1137/0102010 | last1 = O'Brien | first1 = G. G. | title = The Solution of Some Queueing Problems | journal = Journal of the Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics | volume = 2 | issue = 3 | pages = 133–142 | jstor = 2098899| date=September 1954 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal | doi = 10.1287/opre.3.3.255 | last1 = Morse | first1 = P. M. | title = Stochastic Properties of Waiting Lines | journal = Journal of the Operations Research Society of America | volume = 3 | issue = 3 | pages = 255–261 | jstor = 166559| date=August 1955 }}</ref> A second proof of the theorem follows from a more general result published by Reich.<ref>{{Cite journal | last1 = Reich | first1 = Edgar| title = Waiting Times when Queues are in Tandem | journal = The Annals of Mathematical Statistics | volume = 28 | issue = 3 | pages = 768–773 | doi = 10.1214/aoms/1177706889 | year = 1957 | doi-access = free }}</ref> The proof offered by Burke shows that the time intervals between successive departures are independently and exponentially distributed with parameter equal to the arrival rate parameter, from which the result follows.

[[File:Demonstration_Burke_theorem.png|thumb|Trace with departure/arrival instants highlighted in the forward/reversed time process.]]

An alternative proof is possible by considering the [[reversed process]] and noting that the [[M/M/1 queue]] is a reversible stochastic process.<ref name="hui" /> Consider the figure. By [[Kolmogorov's criterion]] for reversibility, any birth-death process is a [[Detailed_balance|reversible Markov chain]]. Note that the arrival instants in the forward Markov chain are the departure instants of the reversed Markov chain. Thus the departure process is a [[Poisson process]] of rate&nbsp;λ. Moreover, in the forward process the arrival at time t is independent of the number of customers after t. Thus in the reversed process, the number of customers in the queue is independent of the departure process prior to time&nbsp;''t''.

This proof could be counter-intuitive, in the sense that the departure process of a birth-death process is independent of the service offered. 
    
==Related results and extensions==
The theorem can be generalised for "only a few cases," but remains valid for [[M/M/c queue]]s and Geom/Geom/1 queues.<ref name="hui">{{Cite book | last1 = Hui | first1 = J. Y. | chapter = Queueing for Multi-Stage Packet Networks | doi = 10.1007/978-1-4615-3264-4_11 | title = Switching and Traffic Theory for Integrated Broadband Networks | series = The Kluwer International Series in Engineering and Computer Science | volume = 91 | pages = 313–341 | year = 1990 | isbn = 978-1-4613-6436-8 }}</ref>

It is thought that Burke's theorem does not extend to queues fed by a [[Markovian arrival process]] (MAP) and is conjectured that the output process of an MAP/M/1 queue is an MAP only if the queue is an M/M/1 queue.<ref>{{Cite journal | last1 = Bean | first1 = Nigel| last2 = Green | first2 = David| last3 = Taylor | first3 = Peter| doi = 10.1239/jap/1032438394 | title = The output process of an MMPP/M/1 queue | journal = Journal of Applied Probability | volume = 35 | issue = 4 | page = 998 | year = 1998 | s2cid = 122137199}}</ref>

An analogous theorem for the [[Brownian queue]] was proven by [[J. Michael Harrison]].<ref name="connell" /><ref>{{cite book|title=Brownian Motion and Stochastic Flow Systems|publisher=Wiley|location=New York|year=1985|first=J. Michael|last=Harrison|author-link=J. Michael Harrison|url=http://faculty-gsb.stanford.edu/harrison/Documents/BrownianMotion-Stochasticms.pdf|access-date=2011-12-01|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120414212149/http://faculty-gsb.stanford.edu/harrison/Documents/BrownianMotion-Stochasticms.pdf|archive-date=2012-04-14}}</ref>
